Gaming PCs are some of the most popular deals this Black Friday, because they're a more economical way to get into PC gaming now that component prices have gone up. Large vendors and OEMs are more insulated from price hikes on SSDs, RAM, and GPUs, and many have existing stock of quality parts. Therefore, buying a gaming PC is often now cheaper than building one by yourself.

That's because 32GB of RAM now costs just over $400, while a 1TB SSD is around $250 at standard market prices. An RTX 5090 is basically impossible to buy, while an RTX 5080 will set you back $2,000. So if you were to buy an RTX 5080 gaming PC, the GPU alone is worth $2,000, before you've added any other parts.

We're tracking all the best prices on gaming PCs at Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and Newegg, using our hands-on testing, reviews, benchmark data, and price tracking to recommend the best deals.

Quick Links: Black Friday gaming PC deals

Amazon: Best gaming PC deals

Newegg: Up to 42% off gaming PCs

Walmart: Up to half price on gaming PCs

Dell: $1,000 off Alienware gaming PCs

A powerful gaming PC from PC building outfit CyberPowerPC, this formidable rig comes equipped with the specs you'll need for serious 1440p and 4K gameplay. It has an AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070, 32GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB NVMe SSD. View Deal

The CyberPower Gamer Xtreme prebuilt PC offers a 20-Core Intel i7 14700F CPU, RTX 5060 Ti GPU, 16GB of DDR5 memory, and 1 TB of storage, wrapped up in a white case, and flush with glowing RGB fans. View Deal

November 27, 2026 – 2:52 AM Welcome to our Black Friday coverage of all the very best gaming PC deals you can buy, now the main event has started we're tracking all the latest and greatest deals! - Stephen Warwick

November 27, 2026 – 2:58 AM Get an RTX 5060 Ti pre-built for just $1,299 — Intel Core i7 14400F, 16GB DDR5, 1TB SSD

Buying a PC on Black Friday doesn't have to mean spending the Earth. If you want a budget build, this Intel Core i7 14700F rig from Cyberpower is a fantastic cheap option for 1080p gaming. With an RTX 5060 Ti 8GB, this should be brilliant for entry-level gaming and could even be pushed to 1440p with Nvidia's DLSS technology.

The CyberPower Gamer Xtreme prebuilt PC offers a 20-Core Intel i7 14700F CPU, RTX 5060 Ti GPU, 16GB of DDR5 memory, and 1 TB of storage, wrapped up in a white case, and flush with glowing RGB fans. View Deal

As you can see from our testing data, in our 19-game testing suite, the RTX 5060 Ti 8GB is good for average frame rates of 72 fps. This drops to around 46 at 1440p without any help from frame generation.

Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future The CPU in this build is Intel's i7 14700F with 20 cores and 28 threads, boasting boost clocks of up to 5.4 GHz- a great processor for productivity and gaming.

Aside from the potent 20-core CPU and GPU for 1080, you also get 16GB of DDR5 RAM and a 1TB SSD. Windows 11 Home comes as standard, and the motherboard supports Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.3. There are also ports aplenty. - Stephen Warwick

November 27, 2026 – 3:29 AM Get a budget gaming PC for 1080p — RTX 5060 with Intel Core i5-14400F now just $1141.99

Buying a gaming PC doesn't have to mean blowing thousands on an RTX 5090 rig with 9950X3D. If you just want something cheap and cheerful for Fortnite, The Sims, or your favorite strategy games, not much more than $1,000 will see you with a nice DDR5 RIG.

Gaming PC, Intel Core i5-14400F, GeForce RTX 5060 8GB: was $1269.75 now $1141.99
Get an RTX 5060 PC with 8GB of VRAM, Intel Core i5-14400F, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB SSD. View Deal

This model comes with Intel's 10-core budget beast, the 14th generation i5-14400F for great gaming performance on a budget. You also get the RTX 5060 GPU, which can put out an average of nearly 65 frames per second in our 19-game test suite at 1080p, and thats without any help from Nvidia's DLSS technology.

Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future This is definitely one of the best budget gaming rigs going right now, and comes from a reputable brand in Cyberpower.

November 27, 2026 – 4:00 AM Get a massive RTX 5090 gaming PC with AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D, $800 off

If you want to buy one monster gaming PC and never think about your rig again, this is the deal for you. This massive Skytech Gaming PC from Best Buy is $800 off and gets you an RTX 5090, 64GB of DDR5, and 4TB of storage.

The RTX 5090 is currently $6,500, making up most of the price of this build, and buying a pre-built is really the only way to get your hands on one right now. 64GB of DDR5 RAM will set you back $1,000 in the current market, while a 4TB SSD is worth $400. As you can see, once you start pricing things up, buying a pre-built looks a lot more enticing in this economy. That's before mentioning the $600 CPU.

Skytech Gaming - Prism 5 Gaming Pc - Amd Ryzen 9 9950x3d (2025) - Nvidia Geforce Rtx 5090 - 64gb Ddr5 Memory - 4tb Storage - Black: was $9799 now $8999
Get an RTX 5090 gaming PC with AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 64GB of DDR5, and 4TB of SSD storage. View Deal

As per our benchmark testing data, the RTX 5090 can pump out nearly 90 fps in 4K with settings in High and even Ultra, all without using DLSS frame generation or upscaling technology. With 32GB of GDDR7 VRAM, it is a monster GPU and the gold-standard for consumer graphics performance in the current market. This will play any title you can throw at it, no questions asked.

Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future The Ryzen 9 9950X3D is a massive 16-core CPU with AMD's 3D V-Cache technology. Not only will it work well for productivity applications, but this is a beastly gaming CPU with almost no downsides. This really is a true do-it-all top-of-the-line gaming PC. - Stephen Warwick

November 27, 2026 – 5:02 AM Get $650 off this budget gaming PC, now just $749

If you want a budget gaming desktop, this is the best option going right now. It's an Intel Core i5 14400F CPU with an RTX 5060 for good 1080p performance. The savings come from the fact that this is a DDR4 PC, rather than DDR5, so the 16GB RAM is a little slower than more modern systems. That being said, this is a very capable rig and a great saving for budget PC buyers.

The ABS Cyclone M Aqua is a midtower gaming PC with an Intel Core i5-14400F, Nvidia RTX 5060, 16GB of DDR4-3200, and a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD. View Deal

ABS is Newegg's in-house PC brand, though this model is shipped and sold by Walmart. Regardless, you can browse the specific components in this rig before buying; ABS doesn't use a grab bag approach to building systems. An important note here, however, is the memory. The machine packs a single 16GB DDR4-3200 DIMM, so you'll want to add a second one for the best performance.

(Image credit: Future) Picking up a second DIMM is reasonable at this price (about $100 for a 16GB DDR4-3200 DIMM) considering the specs and price here. The RTX 5060 is an excellent choice for modern 1080p gaming, able to maintain a 64 FPS average across our demanding 19-game test suite, which includes titles with demanding ray tracing. Plus, it has access to DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution and Multi Frame Generation — though the application of both is limited at 1080p with an 8GB GPU. — Jake Roach

November 27, 2026 – 6:03 AM Another excellent MSI desktop deal — Get $550 off this RTX 5070 gaming desktop

Elsewhere in our deals coverage, we've highlighted this MSI Aegis R2 gaming desktop with a Core Ultra 9 285 CPU and RTX 5070. However, if you want to save even more, you can get it with the Ultra 7 265 for just $2,269, a massive 20% saving.

Aegis R2 Gaming Desktop, Core Ultra 7 265, RTX 5070, 32GB DDR5, 2TB SSD: was $2842.71 now $2269
Get an RTX 5070 gaming PC with 32GB of DDR5 RAM, 2TB SSD, and Core Ultra 7 265 CPU. View Deal

The highlight of this build is the RTX 5070, with 12GB of GDDR7 VRAM and 6,144 CUDA cores, our testing data shows this card can hit more than 40 fps at 4K with no help from DLSS frame generation or upscaling. It will excel at 1440p and 1080p gaming, but it's great to know 4K is an option if you really want it.

Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future The CPU in this build is Intel's 265. This ARrow Lake CPU is a 20-core, 20-thread CPU with 8 performance and 12 efficiency cores. It will excel at multithreaded performance for desktop productivity, and sits in the ballpark between the Ryzen 5 7600X and Ryzen 7 7700X in terms of gaming performance in our testing data. It's not monster AMD X3D SKU, but should be more than capable.

A real highlight of this build is the 32GB of DDR5 RAM, an increasing rarity in pre-builts, as well as a generous 2TB SSD, whereas you'd mostly expect to find 1TB at this price point. - Stephen Warwick

November 27, 2026 – 7:05 AM One of my favorite Black Friday PCs — get an RTX 5080 rig for $2,699

One of my favorite gaming PC deals of the sales so far is this unassuming Omen 35L. It comes with an RTX 5080. That GPU alone is $2,000 in today's market, but this PC is just $2,699.99 in total.

OMEN 35L Gaming Desktop: was $4399.99 now $2699.99
Get an RTX 5080 PC from HP's HyperX gaming brand with Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, 16GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD, with plenty of space to upgrade. Also features Wi-Fi 7. View Deal

As you can see from our testing data, the RTX 5080 with its 16GB of GDDR7 VRAM is a fully-fledged 4K gaming GPU, cruising 60 fps in our testing suite with no help from DLSS.

Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future Future You also get Intel's new (and really quite fantastic) Ultra 7 270K Plus. This 24-core, 24-thread CPU is a productivity beast and Intel's best CPU for gaming by some distance. Our testing data shows that in gaming performance it gives the Core i9-14900K a run for its money, and isn't far behind AMD's 7800X3D for fps.

You get a 1TB SSD for storing your games, and 16GB of RAM. The RAM capacity is really the only downside, but the rest of the rig is such good value you could get this, buy 32GB of DDR5, and still come out on top.

Other features include Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0, and a ton of ports, as well as plenty of motherboard slots for SSD expansion. - Stephen Warwick
